tests.notes: a negative literal is folded at compile time, so -128 is accepted for int8 even though +128 would not fit
-(-x) and - -x both return x; the first negation of type(int256).min reverts with Panic(0x11); without the space -- would be a decrement
a - -b is a + b, a + -b is a - b, a * -b is -(a * b); the space between operators matters
++x yields the new value: f(5) == (6, 6)
x++ yields the old value and increments afterwards: f(5) == (5, 6)
--x yields the new value: f(5) == (4, 4)
x-- yields the old value and decrements afterwards: f(5) == (5, 4)
prefix and postfix ++ and -- on a storage variable follow the same old-vs-new rule; dec() on a zero counter reverts with Panic(0x11)
a missing key reads as 0, so the first prefix increment yields 1 and the first postfix increment returns 0
++ and -- on a storage array element and on struct fields including a narrow packed uint8 field
compiles successfully; ++ and -- cross zero correctly and inc(127) / dec(-128) revert with Panic(0x11)
for-loop counter, while loop counting down, and do-while counting up
a[i++] reads the element at the old index and then advances the index: readTwo() == (10, 20, 2)
delete assigns the default value 0 on both local and storage integers
delete resets bool to false, address to address(0), bytesN to zero bytes and enum to its first member
deleting an element resets it but keeps the length; deleting the whole dynamic array sets its length to 0
deleting a fixed-size storage array resets every element; the length is unchanged
deleting a struct resets all of its fields to their defaults
deleting a struct resets every field except mappings, which keep their entries
a single mapping entry can be deleted by key; other keys are unaffected
deleting a storage string or bytes resets it to empty
unary minus exists only for signed integers; applying it to unsigned is rejected since 0.8.0
unary minus does not apply to bool
++ and -- apply to integers only
++ does not apply to address; it would need a round trip through uint160
a constant cannot be modified by ++ or by any other operator
delete needs a location to reset; a computed value is not an lvalue
a mapping cannot be deleted as a whole because its keys cannot be enumerated; delete individual entries (see 021)
calldata is read-only, so a calldata array element cannot be modified in place
